name: site.disable
description: Retire one site without deleting anything. It takes every enabled nginx file serving the root out of nginx (a sites-enabled symlink is removed; a regular file in sites-enabled or conf.d is moved to /etc/nginx/bifrost-disabled), runs nginx -t and reloads; comments out cron lines (/etc/cron.d, users' crontabs) that run anything under the root, with a marker; sets supervisor programs whose command or directory is under the root to autostart=false and stops them; and disables and stops systemd services whose ExecStart or WorkingDirectory is under the root. Files, databases, certificates, DNS, the firewall and PHP-FPM pools are left alone. It refuses when a file serving the root also serves another root, or is a default_server. Each change is recorded with what was there before in /var/lib/bifrost-agent/disabled-sites, which site.enable replays. It checks afterwards that no enabled vhost serves the root and the programs and units are stopped; on any failure it puts back everything it changed. The dry run (the site_plan state tool) lists what will change, and drift: a vhost serving the root again after it was disabled.

root.description: The site's app root, the directory above public/, such as /home/acme/example.com.

vhost.description: The nginx file the site was seen in, a hint only: the agent checks it serves root, and finds the right files itself.

health_check: The helper checks nginx -t passes, no enabled vhost serves the root, and the stopped programs and units are inactive, and puts everything back if not.
